A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Scale-invariant attention work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training, needle-in-a-haystack retrieval, entropy simulations, and attention-logit analyses in Section 4 and Appendices H-J.

after.justification: v2 retains original training and retrieval results and adds Infini-Attention comparisons, Llama-2 7B continual-pretraining results, and expanded Gaussianity diagnostics.

M1.justification: The position-dependent logit transformation in Equations 14-16, its boundary conditions, the selected lengthscale, and its combination with p-RoPE remain unchanged. The added larger-model experiment applies this mechanism without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb language modeling, C4-based needle-in-a-haystack retrieval, and the same Wikipedia introduction for logit analysis. The additions change models, comparators, and experimental procedures without adding datasets or task requirements. Language-model evaluation lengths remain 4k, 16k, and 64k.

E2.justification: YaRN changes from cited prior work to an evaluated comparator in Tables 1-2 and Figures 3 and 7. New Table 3 compares Infini-RoPE and Infini-p-RoPE against RoPE and the proposed method. These additions substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives, including a KV-cache compression approach.

E3.justification: Appendix I.5 adds continual pretraining of Llama-2 7B on approximately 50M FineWeb tokens at 4k, followed by evaluation at 4k/16k/64k. This extends the original small-model training protocols; Table 4 explicitly leaves RoPE and RoPE+NTK unfine-tuned. Appendix J also introduces different model configurations and paired diagnostics with and without RoPE.

E4.justification: Appendix J replaces the single-model Llama-3B Gaussianity check with checks for Llama-1B, Llama-8B, and Gemma 2 27B, each with and without RoPE. This substantially expands scrutiny of the distributional assumption and adds a positional-encoding control. The lengthscale sweep, entropy analyses, and alternative scale-invariant attention ablations remain.

E5.justification: Tables 1-2 retain means and one standard error across three seeds; new Table 3 uses the same reporting convention. Appendix G's run-count statements are unchanged. Table 4 supplies point estimates without uncertainty or a specific seed count, but no uncertainty treatment for retained experiments or statistical estimation procedure is revised.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1-2 retain their values. Added YaRN results include 64k loss 5.353 ± 0.065 and retrieval accuracy 0.000 ± 0.000. Table 3 adds 64k losses of 3.310 ± 0.008 for Infini-RoPE and 3.311 ± 0.009 for Infini-p-RoPE, versus the retained proposed-method result of 3.247 ± 0.001. New Table 4 reports proposed-method 7B losses of 2.163/2.193/2.252 at 4k/16k/64k; these are new-setting results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 and Theorem 1, including its Appendix F restatement, drop the independence requirement while retaining Gaussian marginals. This broadens the theorem's stated applicability. The definitions, transformation, and proof remain unchanged; the existing argument already uses marginal moments and linearity of expectation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about scale-invariance conditions, the logit transformation, improved long-context language modeling, and effective retrieval. The new experiments provide additional support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 now distinguishes small-model pretraining from the added 7B continual-pretraining study while retaining the limitation concerning training large models from scratch. Appendix I.5 explains the choice of Llama-2 and discusses the short-context cost of modifying attention alongside the long-context advantage.

D1.justification: Appendix I.5 documents Torchtune, AdamW, and a learning rate of 2 × 10^-5; Table 4 specifies approximately 50M training tokens. Appendix J clarifies use of the lower-triangular query-key products, while omitting v1's explicit 454-token input length. Existing hardware, implementation, and code/data access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Llama-2, Gemma 2, and Torchtune. Appendix I.4 gives additional positioning of the already-cited Infini-Attention as a KV-cache compression method. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning relative to LogN remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized rewrites of the limitations and Appendix J, new Appendix I.4-I.5 subsections, acknowledgements, and replacement of the preprint footer with the NeurIPS 2025 designation.

P2.justification: New Tables 3-4 and six Gaussianity figures substantially expand the visual evidence, replacing v1's single QQ figure. Tables 1-2 and Figures 3 and 7 gain YaRN rows, curves, and legends. Figures 2 and 6 are recolored, and several plots are resized and appendix material relocated.

improvement.justification: The 7B experiment substantially narrows v1's acknowledged gap between small-model performance evidence and applicability to larger LLMs. Additional baseline comparisons and broader Gaussianity diagnostics strengthen the empirical support, while removing the unnecessary independence assumption improves theoretical precision. The larger-model evidence remains limited to continual pretraining, lacks reported uncertainty, and includes two unfine-tuned controls. These limitations constrain its interpretation but do not outweigh the substantial gain in direct evidence.
